charges: and a 31-year-old man with serious head injuries is life-flighted to another state’s hospital. Down the alley on East Roosevelt, a victim’s purse is covered in blood. Officers later find the purse victim with her teeth knocked out; the woman says she has no idea who assaulted her. Welcome to a Thursday night for the Riverton Police. It’s not uncommon for warm weather to spice up police blotters, but Fremont County has experienced a spike in violence — including deadly violence — in 2024. There were three violent deaths recorded in January and February, and two men were shot last weekend. It’s left some residents wondering: What is happening? Riverton resident Jose Proos was angry after the weekend shooting, which occurred near his home where his children live. He said he has contacted the police chief and mayor multiple times about drug activity at the residence where the two men reportedly suffered non-life threatening injuries. One, the resident, was reportedly airlifted to a Wyoming hospital. Proos said he had called police for weeks about alleged drug activity at the residence in the All Nations subdivision where the shooting occurred. On Monday, Riverton City Administrator Kyle Butterfield and Riverton Police Chief Eric Hurtado visited Proos to discuss his concerns. “It is a pretty city … especially when you can’t even get a hold of you (the police) for three weeks on a non-emergency line,” he told Hurtado on Monday morning. “When I’m calling you guys and telling you about a drug dealer, and he gets shot” in a residential neighborhood, with young children living in at least one of the nearby homes, “they’re lucky that guy didn’t have two (bullets).” Hurtado pointed out that the way Proos’ calls were phrased may have made it seem as though his concerns were to do with someone driving around the neighborhood in the early hours of the morning rather than safety or trespassing. “When you put my family and my neighbors’ families in danger and we can’t even talk to you … This is an ongoing deal,” Proo said. The problem is, Jose, there’s only a few of us,” Hurtado responded. “If we’re going call to call and people are getting hurt, we have to prioritize.” Due to ongoing problems with crime in the neighborhood, Proos and many of his neighbors have surveillance cameras outside their homes; on Monday, Hurtado and Butterfield asked them to provide any footage from the night of the shooting. Fremont County murders by the numbers This year isn’t an anomaly in fatal violence for the county, but with three deaths attributed to violence in the first two months, it’s statistically on track to break records. That’s according to Fremont County Coroner’s Office data tracking the last 10 years of homicide here. During the past decade, 2014 included the most murders by far, with a dozen. That’s about triple the national average for areas with similar populations, according to the National Statistic Comparison from CDC — National Vital Statistics System. That year, half of the state’s homicides occurred in Fremont County. But since that year homicides have trended down in Fremont County, with eight in 2015, nine in 2016 and 2017, two in 2018, seven in 2019, five in 2020, two in 2021, and three in both 2022 and 2023. A violent weekend Between March 2-5, Riverton Police and the Fremont County Sheriff’s Office responded to three reports of stabbing or gunshots, including the one near Proos’ All Nations home that left two men suffering from gunshot wounds. According to Riverton Police, officers responded to a report of a shooting near Comanche and Arapahoe drives just after 4 a.m. on Sunday and found a 61-year-old resident suffering from a gunshot wound. The sheriff’s office and Bureau of Indian Affairs also responded to the scene. Officers later contacted a 60-year-old male who also reported being struck by gunfire during an argument at a residence near Comanche Drive. Both are being treated in Wyoming hospitals; one was life-flighted to a larger medical center in the state. Anyone with information about the incident is encouraged to contact detectives at 307-856-4891.
